name: Dominican Slang
description: Real Dominican street Spanish. Starter deck, more to come.

cards.example_en: What's up, my buddy! All good?
cards.notes: Written "klk" in texts. Said fast: "keh-loh-KEH".

cards.example_en: Pass me that thing.
cards.notes: Means almost anything. "¡Qué vaina!" = What a mess!

cards.example_en: That party was awesome.
cards.notes: From English "heavy".

cards.example_en: That guy's a hustler.
cards.notes: Can be a compliment (smart, smooth) or a warning (a player).

cards.example_en: So tell me, what happened last night?

cards.example: No puedo salir, estoy en olla.
cards.example_en: I can't go out, I'm broke.

cards.example: Él es mi pana desde la escuela.
cards.example_en: He's been my buddy since school.
"See you at eight?" "Alright."
Give me a little bit of rice.
cards.notes: Also "chin chin" = a tiny tiny bit.

cards.example: Hoy es un corito sano, nada de bochinche.
cards.example_en: Today's a chill hangout, no drama.

cards.english: Do I speak Chinese? (I don't get it)
cards.example: ¿Yo hablo chino? Te dije que no.
cards.example_en: Am I speaking Chinese? I told you no.
cards.notes: Said when someone isn't getting what you mean.

cards.example: Yo estoy rulay en la casa.
cards.example_en: I'm chilling at home.

cards.example: ¡Vamo' a darle, que se hace tarde!
cards.example_en: Let's go, it's getting late!
cards.notes: Dropped s: "vamos" → "vamo'".

cards.example: Ella priva en rica, pero vive en olla.
cards.example_en: She acts rich, but she's always broke.
cards.notes: Also heard as "privar en" / "privar de" + adjective.

cards.example_en: I don't want any drama today.
What are you doing here so late?
cards.notes: Caribbean word order puts "tú" before the verb. Standard: ¿Qué haces tú?

cards.example_en: "Shall we go to the beach?" "Let's go!"

cards.example: ¿Qué e' lo que hay, mi hermano?
cards.example_en: What's up, bro?
cards.notes: Long form of "¿Qué lo qué?".

cards.example_en: Don't be lame, ask her to dance.
cards.notes: Said to come from "party watcher": the guy who just stands and watches at the party.

cards.example_en: Last night was a lot of fun.
cards.notes: "Estar en chercha" = to be joking around.

cards.example: Hoy hay [teteo] en casa de Luis.
cards.example_en: There's a party at Luis's place today.
cards.notes: Young people's slang. "Tetear" = to party.

cards.example_en: Let's hang out tonight.
cards.notes: "Coro" = a hangout or your crew.

cards.example_en: I'm going to the corner store to buy ice.
cards.notes: The Dominican neighborhood shop: drinks, music, dominoes, gossip. Like a "bodega" in NYC.

cards.example_en: I took the bus downtown.
cards.notes: Used in DR, Puerto Rico and Cuba. In the Caribbean "coger" is a normal word (take/catch).

cards.example_en: I took a shared taxi to work.
cards.notes: "Motoconcho" = motorcycle taxi.

cards.example_en: That's my girl.
cards.notes: For a guy: "jevo" = boyfriend / dude.

cards.example: Ese tipo es un [jablador], no le creas.
cards.example_en: That guy's full of it, don't believe him.
cards.notes: From "hablador" with the Dominican "j" sound.

cards.example_en: That kid is out of control.
cards.notes: From "desacatado" with the dropped d (-ado → -ao).

cards.example: No seas [allantoso] con tu carro nuevo.
cards.example_en: Don't be a show-off with your new car.
cards.notes: "Hacer allante" = to show off.

cards.example_en: Your car is cool.
cards.notes: Also big in Colombia.

cards.example: Había una [pila] de gente en la fiesta.
cards.example_en: There were tons of people at the party.
Damn, that's expensive!
cards.notes: A softened "diablo". Safe to say around family.

cards.example_en: I had mangú with salami for breakfast.
cards.notes: With fried salami, cheese and eggs it is "los tres golpes".

cards.example_en: Can you give me a banana?
cards.notes: Most of Latin America says "plátano" or "banana".

cards.example: Le dicen [cuero], pero eso es un insulto feo.
cards.example_en: They call her a "cuero", but that's an ugly insult.
cards.notes: Literally "leather". Offensive. Know it, don't use it.

cards.example_en: That c*cksucker hit my car!
cards.notes: One of the strongest Dominican insults. Also spelled "mamagüebo".
